segments.text:
Usage text of the tool. `main` shows it as the help text (line 90).
- One process in the file is one header line that starts with `-- binary`, then the output of the benchmark binary: one comment line, one line of column names, one line per timed interval and one `best` line.
- The tool reports the column `aggregate_GBps` per pair of kernel and binary. GB means 1e9 bytes.

`HDR` is the pattern of a header line. ra.sh (the script of part A) writes one header line directly before it starts a benchmark process. The eight groups are, in this order: binary, kernel, thread count, CPU list, buffer size, round, load and UTC time. A header line without the `utc` part also fits.

Open `threads120.csv` of the folder and read it line by line. `ln` is the line number, counted from 1. `strip` removes spaces and the line end from both ends of the line. `procs` collects one record per process, and `cur` is the process that the next interval lines belong to.
segments.heading: Function `load`: read the processes of one folder

segments.text: A line that fits `HDR` starts a new process record. The record keeps the folder, the binary, the kernel, the round, the load, the UTC time and an empty list `iv` for the intervals. The thread count, the CPU list and the buffer size of the header line are not kept.

Every other line is split at the commas into the list `p`. Python counts from 0, so `p[3]` is field 4, `rep`. The line is an interval line when it has more than 8 fields and field 4 holds digits only. This test drops the `#` comment line (it has no comma), the line of column names (field 4 is the word `rep`) and the `best` line (field 4 is `best`).

- An interval line must come after a header line, and its first field must be the kernel of that header line. If not, the script stops and names the file and the line.
- Kept per interval: `p[6]` = `aggregate_GBps`, `p[7]` = `per_thread_min_GBps`, `p[8]` = `per_thread_max_GBps`. The last two are the lowest and the highest rate of one thread in the interval. The rate of a thread is its bytes divided by its own elapsed time [Ref1].
- Also kept: the pass count `p[4] // p[2]`. It is `total_bytes` divided by `bytes_per_thread`, rounded down.
- Not read: `p[1]` (`threads`), `p[5]` (`elapsed_s`) and `p[9]` (`per_thread_avg_GBps`).
- No rate is computed here. `aggregate_GBps` is the number that the binary printed: the bytes of all threads, divided by the longest elapsed time of one thread, divided by 1e9 [Ref1].
The script stops when the file holds no header line. Otherwise `load` returns the processes in file order.

`loads` holds the load of every process that was passed in. `cells` groups the processes by the pair (kernel, binary), in the order in which each pair first appears. So the old read kernel is the group (`read`, `bw_old`), and the new read kernel is the group (`read`, `bw_new`).
segments.heading: Function `rows_of`: statistics per kernel and binary

segments.text: `iv` lists every interval of the group: the intervals of its first process, then those of the next process. No interval is left out. `v` holds the `aggregate_GBps` values of these intervals.

One result row per group, computed over `v`:
- `n`: the number of intervals. `min` and `max`: the lowest and the highest `aggregate_GBps`.
- `median`: the middle value. For an even `n` it is the mean of the two middle values. It is rounded to 3 decimals (0.001 GB/s).
- `values`, `rounds`, `per_thread_min`, `per_thread_max`, `passes`: one entry per interval, in file order.
- `processes` and `loads`: the number of processes of the group and their load values.
- `folder_load_min` and `folder_load_max`: the lowest and the highest load over all processes that were passed in, not only those of this group.
A pooled row also names its folders. `_procs` keeps the process records for the text report. `main` removes this field before the JSON output (line 108).

Print the title, one summary line and one line that describes the layout of the report. The summary line holds the number of processes, the different interval counts per process, and the lowest and the highest load. The load values are taken from the first row, and they are the same in every row of the group.
segments.heading: Function `print_text`: text report of one group

segments.text: Print one line per pair of kernel and binary: `n`, then `min`, `median` and `max` with 2 decimals (0.01 GB/s). A pair without an interval prints `NO INTERVAL`. Under it, print one line per process: round, load, UTC time, and for each interval the rate, the per-thread minimum and maximum and the pass count. In a pooled report the line starts with the folder name.
Read the arguments: any number of folders, `--pool` with any number of folders after it, and `--json`.
segments.heading: Function `main`: arguments, statistics, output

segments.text:
- `norm` removes `/` characters from the end of a folder name.
- `singles` is the list of all folders named anywhere on the command line, each one once. The folders outside `--pool` come first, then the folders after `--pool`. Without a folder the script ends with a usage error.
- `pool` is the list of the folders to pool: the folders after `--pool`, or all folders when none follows `--pool`. Without `--pool` the list is empty.

Read every folder once with `load`. Build one group of rows per folder with `rows_of`. With a pool, join the processes of the pool folders and build one more group from them. Its rows carry the folder label `pool`.
With `--json`, print the rows of all groups as one JSON list, without the field `_procs`. Without it, print each group with `print_text`.
After the output, list every process that has a header line and no interval line. If the list is not empty, the script prints it as an error message and ends with exit status 1.
Run `main` when the file is started as a script. When another script imports the file, `main` does not run.
